propositions: Negative caplog assertions pass vacuously when no records are captured, silently losing test coverage without failing or signaling in output.
Process-global logger configuration (propagate=False or raised level) in production code poisons downstream tests, making their log assertions unreachable while appearing to pass.
The void window is one test phase wide; log assertions can verify nothing in a given run while passing green, with no way to distinguish from genuine coverage using only the exit code.
Five negative caplog assertions in the test suite were verified as reachable and currently working, but the mechanism enabling their failure is order-dependent and silent when broken.
An autouse fixture guard detects and fails tests when logger.propagate is disabled, catching poisoning at its source rather than at random victim tests downstream.
The guard also restores logger level at test teardown to contain the effect of in-process entrypoint calls, ensuring each test starts with the same baseline regardless of run order.
